Anonymous theorem reconstruction

This is a reconstruction of the supplied anonymous statement and approved definitions only. It does not identify a source or assess proof correctness or source fidelity.

Inputs and their exact scope

E is any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive commutative group structure, a measurable space and a BorelSpace instance. Zero dimension is permitted. V:E→ℝ is arbitrary subject to ContDiff ℝ 2 V and the displayed global second-derivative bounds. α and β are nonnegative real numbers (ℝ≥0), while η is a real number. The explicit additional assumptions are 0<(α:ℝ), α≤β, 0<η, (β:ℝ)η≤1, and, for every x,v∈E,
  (α:ℝ)‖v‖² ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β:ℝ)‖v‖².
The derivative is the iterated Fréchet derivative evaluated twice at v; both bounds are global, including v=0. There is no premise that μ,J,ν are probability measures, no public closedness certificate, no public range equality, no public kernel, operator, square root, normalization or integrability certificate. No stronger smoothness order, positive dimension, zero-mean restriction or strict inequality βη<1 is imposed. The endpoint βη=1 is included. Positivity of β follows at the level of input arithmetic from α>0 and α≤β; it is not an extra binder.

Constructed measures, sigma algebra and spaces

μ is normalized exponential tilting of volume on E by −V: in normalized-density notation its weight is exp(−V(x)), divided by its integral. J is the pushforward of μ⊗stdGaussian(E) under (x,z)↦(x,x+√η z), where multiplication by √η is scalar multiplication in E. Thus its two coordinates can be denoted X,Y. ν=J.snd is the Y marginal. Λ is the pushforward of J under (x,y)↦(y,2x−y). F is a different map on the original joint-coordinate space: F(x,y)=(x,2x−y). It keeps the first coordinate fixed, whereas Λ's defining map puts y in its first coordinate. These two maps must not be conflated.

The product E×E carries its usual product measurable-space instance. mY=comap(Prod.snd) of E's measurable space is the sigma algebra generated by the second coordinate. The local Fact(mY≤product) is explicitly constructed from measurable_snd.comap_le inside the statement. It is an internal instance supporting closedness of the displayed measurable subspace, as specified by the approved context; it is not a universal or existential input certificate. The statement then defines H=Lp ℝ 2 J, K=Lp ℝ 2 ν and HP=lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J, a closed real linear subspace of H consisting of classes measurable with respect to mY. All these L² spaces contain measurable square-integrable almost-everywhere equivalence classes, with their complete real Hilbert-space structures. HP elements are subtypes with inclusion i=HP.subtypeL:HP→H; HP is not the entire joint space and is not K as a definitional identity.

P:H→H is i composed with L² conditional expectation onto HP. Its defining conditional expectation uses the internally supplied comap inequality. It therefore returns an ambient joint-space class after inclusion. hp is the internal measure-preserving witness for Prod.snd:(E×E,J)→(E,ν), with measurable_snd and the definitional pushforward identity rfl. M:K→H is the canonical real linear isometric pullback along this projection. M is an embedding, not yet a stipulated onto equivalence.

Initial conclusions and the normalized kernel

The theorem concludes that μ,J,ν are all probability measures; that HP=P.toLinearMap.range as subspaces of H; and that for every f∈HP, P(i f)=i f in H. The range equality is stronger than mere containment and is an output, not a hypothesis.

There exists a kernel S:E→measures(E) that is Markov and, for every state y∈E (without an almost-everywhere qualifier), equals normalized exponential tilting of volume by
  x↦−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η).
Equivalently the displayed normalized density is proportional to exp(−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)) with its state-dependent normalization. The equality is equality of measures at every state, and no separate supplied normalization premise occurs. The same S is a conditional kernel for Λ, with Λ.fst=ν and Λ.snd=ν. These are stationary disintegration/marginal conclusions about Λ, not a pointwise identity of conditional-expectation representatives and not a claim that Λ=J. The generic disintegration relation and the every-state chosen normalized kernel must remain distinct.

Canonical identification and reflection

For this kernel witness there exists a real linear isometric equivalence e:K≃HP such that for every u∈K, i(e u)=M u in H. The equality fixes e to the canonical second-coordinate pullback after inclusion, rather than permitting an unrelated abstract Hilbert-space equivalence. Both its surjectivity onto HP and this canonical compatibility are conclusions.

There exists a real linear isometry U:H→H for which, for every g∈H, the representative of U g equals g∘F J-almost everywhere. The quantifier order is ∀g, AE_J; the statement does not require one exceptional set working simultaneously for all observables. U is involutive (U(U g)=g for every joint-space class g) and its associated continuous linear endomorphism is selfadjoint. This literal reflection action is on H, not directly on K or HP. Its class-level involution and selfadjointness are exact identities, whereas the representative composition formula is almost everywhere.

Conditional observable operator

There exists T:K→K, a real continuous linear endomorphism, selfadjoint, such that for every u∈K all three properties hold:
  ‖T u‖≤‖u‖;
  (T u)(y)=∫x,u(x) dS(y)(x) for ν-almost every y;
  ∫y,(T u)(y) dν(y)=∫y,u(y) dν(y).
The second property is per-observable almost-everywhere equality of representatives, not an everywhere action formula. The integral identity is an equality of scalar integrals. No extra mean-zero hypothesis or pointwise common-null-set premise is present. Positivity of T is not stated; selfadjoint contraction is the displayed property.

Compression, leakage and all operator domains

With e,U,T already chosen, define q=HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto:H→HP, and define
  A=q∘U∘i : HP→HP;
  B=((I_H−P) U P)∘i : HP→H.
Here juxtaposition/operator multiplication means composition, acting right to left. Thus B first includes f into H, applies P, then U, then I_H−P. The identity I_H and P and U in this expression are ambient joint-space endomorphisms. A instead returns a macro/subspace class through the orthogonal projection. The theorem asserts A=e T e⁻¹ as continuous linear endomorphisms of HP, using e.conjStarAlgEquiv, and IsSelfAdjoint A. For every f∈HP, ‖A f‖≤‖f‖, and for every f∈HP, P(B f)=0 in H. The latter is ambient conditional-projection annihilation of the leakage output; it does not say B=0.

There exists Γ:K→K, a positive real continuous linear operator, such that
  ΓΓ=I_K−TT.
Positivity means selfadjointness and nonnegative quadratic form, by the approved definition context. Γ is an internally produced operator on the marginal observable L² space, not a real-valued scalar. Calling it the marginal root distinguishes its domain; there is no extra square-root input or spectral certificate.

Let ΓP=e Γ e⁻¹:HP→HP. This macro root is defined by transporting that SAME Γ. It is not an independent existential witness. The theorem asserts ΓP is positive and
  ΓPΓP=I_HP−AA;
  B*∘B=ΓPΓP.
In the second equality B*:H→HP is the adjoint of B:HP→H, so B*∘B is an endomorphism of HP. It cannot be equated to an operator on H or K without the stated adapters. The identities I_K, I_HP and I_H act on three different domains. ΓΓ, TT, ΓPΓP and AA are composition squares, not pointwise products of representatives. All these operator equalities hold exactly at the operator/class level.

For every macro class f∈HP the following two energy/norm identities hold together:
  ‖B f‖=‖ΓP f‖;
  ‖ΓP f‖²=‖f‖²−‖A f‖².
The B norm is the norm in H, while the ΓP,A and f norms use HP's inherited Hilbert norm. Every macro class is included; there is no mean, smoothness or energy-class restriction beyond membership in HP.

Finally, for EVERY continuous real linear operator G:HP→HP, if G is positive and GG=I_HP−AA, then G=ΓP. This universal alternative-operator quantifier is a separate final conjunct outside the ∀f energy assertion. It is not nested under an individual f and has no premise that G obeys a matching energy identity. Its only two hypotheses are positivity and equality of its square to I_HP−AA. In particular the displayed uniqueness claim is on HP; a separate universal uniqueness clause on K for Γ is not literally stated.

All input type/instance/parameter binders precede the named assumptions. The measure, sigma-algebra, internal Fact, Hilbert-space, P,hp,M lets are internal constructions. Probability, range and fixed-subspace assertions precede the nested existential witnesses. The witness order is S, then e, then U, then T, then Γ, with A and B defined after T and ΓP defined after Γ.
